learn.title: Floating Solar Farms on Water
learn.intro: As land becomes scarce, we are looking to the water! Floating solar, or 'floatovoltaics,' offers a brilliant way to generate clean energy without competing with agriculture for precious land. This technology turns reservoirs and lakes into power plants while simultaneously protecting our most vital resource: water.
learn.c1_text: Instead of using fertile farmland, we float panels on water. Think of it like using a swimming pool for a party instead of taking up the living room floor. This saves space for crops and reduces land-use conflicts in densely populated regions.
learn.c2_text: The panels act like a giant sunshade. By covering parts of reservoirs, they reduce evaporation. This keeps water levels higher for drinking and irrigation, much like how a lid on a pot keeps steam from escaping while cooking.
learn.c3_text: Water provides a natural cooling effect for the panels. Since solar cells work better when they are cool, this setup can increase efficiency compared to land-based arrays, a trend being watched closely by global energy planners.

learn.title: Rooftop Solar and Net Metering in India
learn.intro: Transforming your roof into a mini power plant is a game-changer for India's energy landscape. By using rooftop solar, homes and businesses can reduce their reliance on the grid and lower electricity bills, contributing directly to India's massive renewable energy goals.
learn.c1_text: Solar panels on your roof capture sunlight and convert it into DC electricity. An inverter then turns it into AC electricity for your appliances. It is like having a personal garden that grows electricity instead of vegetables.
learn.c2_text: Net metering is a billing mechanism. When your panels produce more power than you use, the excess flows back to the grid. Think of it like a bank account where you deposit energy credits to use later.
learn.c3_text: The MNRE encourages rooftop solar through various subsidies and net-metering policies. This allows Indian households to become 'prosumers'—both producers and consumers—helping decentralize the national power grid.

learn.title: Green Steel and Hydrogen Production
learn.intro: Steel is the backbone of modern civilization, but traditional production is a massive carbon polluter. Transitioning to 'Green Steel' using hydrogen is essential to decarbonizing heavy industry and meeting global net-zero targets.
learn.c1_text: Traditional blast furnaces use coal (coke) to strip oxygen from iron ore, releasing huge amounts of CO2. It is like burning wood in a fireplace to make heat, but the smoke is the byproduct we want to avoid.
learn.c2_text: In green steel production, hydrogen replaces coal. Instead of emitting CO2, the chemical reaction produces only pure water vapor. This turns a high-emission process into a clean, circular cycle.
learn.c3_text: Global steel production is responsible for roughly 7-9% of CO2 emissions. Moving to hydrogen-based Direct Reduced Iron (DRI) is the primary pathway for the industry to reach zero-emissions targets.

learn.title: How Hydrogen Fuel Cells Work
learn.intro: Hydrogen fuel cells offer a way to power heavy vehicles without the weight of massive batteries. They provide the range of traditional fuels with the cleanliness of an electric motor, making them vital for the future of transport.
learn.c1_text: A fuel cell combines hydrogen from a tank with oxygen from the air. This reaction creates electricity through a chemical process. It's like a battery that never runs out as long as you keep adding fuel.
learn.c2_text: Unlike combustion engines that burn fuel, fuel cells use an electrochemical process. The only byproduct is pure water (H2O). This means the exhaust pipe of a fuel cell vehicle emits only clean water vapor.
learn.c3_text: While batteries are great for small cars, hydrogen is ideal for heavy trucks and buses. It offers faster refueling times and higher energy density, which is crucial for long-haul logistics and heavy-duty transport sectors.

learn.title: India's National Green Hydrogen Mission
learn.intro: India is positioning itself as a global leader in the hydrogen economy. The National Green Hydrogen Mission is a strategic roadmap to create a massive ecosystem for producing and using clean hydrogen across various industrial sectors.
learn.c1_text: The mission aims to make India a global hub for green hydrogen production. It focuses on scaling up electrolyzer manufacturing and creating a robust supply chain, much like building a highway for a new type of fuel.
learn.c2_text: To encourage companies to switch from gray to green hydrogen, the government provides financial incentives. This lowers the 'green premium,' making it cost-competitive with traditional, fossil-fuel-based hydrogen production.
learn.c3_text: This mission targets sectors like refineries, fertilizer, and steel. By scaling green hydrogen, India aims to reduce its massive fossil fuel import bill and meet its 2030 renewable energy capacity targets.

learn.title: The Power of Solid-State Batteries
learn.intro: The next revolution in electric vehicles lies in the chemistry of the battery. Solid-state batteries promise to solve the biggest hurdles for EV adoption: range anxiety, charging time, and safety concerns.
learn.c1_text: Current batteries use liquid electrolytes. Solid-state batteries use a solid material. Imagine replacing a sloshing water tank with a solid block of gel; it is much more stable and less prone to leaking or catching fire.
learn.c2_text: Because they are more compact, solid-state batteries can store much more energy in the same amount of space. This means EVs can travel much further on a single charge—potentially doubling current ranges.
learn.c3_text: Solid electrolytes are much less flammable than liquid ones. This makes batteries safer during high-speed charging or in the event of a collision, significantly reducing the risk of thermal runaway in electric vehicles.
